Risk:
Insurance Risk – The risk that the
claims and premium liabilities esti-
mated are higher than actual claims
that the company ends up settling.
Source of Risk:
Life Insurance
• Longevity
• Persistency
• Mortality and Morbidity
• Expenses
Health Insurance
• Underwriting
• Expenses
• Reserving
We take measured amounts on both life and health
insurance risks in line with our core skills in underwriting
and pricing.
Mitigation:
Effective underwriting and reinsurance strategies mitigate
exposure to claim volatility and catastrophic events.
Additional supporting structures include:
• Robust product development frameworks which
generate products that meet customer needs.
• Rollout of policyholder engagements and retention
strategies.
• Extensive use of data and financial models to improve
pricing.
• Implementation of robust expense management
initiatives.
• Retention of additional capital, guided by Risk Based
Capital (RBC) guidelines, that shield the company
against this risk.

Risk:
Market & Investment Risk
– Risks that financial assets held re-
duce in value below their expected
long-term values.
Source of Risk:
Inherent risks include:
• Property investments return
• Interest Rates
• Equity Prices
• Foreign Exchange Fluctuations
Mitigation:
Investment Policies in place guiding portfolio diversification
and liability-driven asset allocation strategies to reduce the
impact of market fluctuations. Appropriate benchmarks set
for the investment managers.

Risk:
Liquidity & Capital Adequacy
Risk – Risk that the business cannot
meet its obligations as and when
they fall due.
Source of Risk:
• Mismatch of assets and liabilities, usually by
duration and amounts.
• Low generation of cashflow. Might be due to
reduced inflows and elevated withdrawals.
Mitigation:
Stringent liquidity and capital management practices ensure
that JHL can meet its financial obligations under stressed
scenarios.
They include:
• Asset Liability Matching (ALM) policy that ensures as-
sets and labilities are matched by amounts, currency,
duration and nature.
• Contingency funding plan to be put in place to ad-
dress funding requirements in stressed scenarios.
• Holding sufficient capital buffers above regulatory
minimums.

Risk:
Counterparty and Credit Risks
– Risks that counterparties may
not be able to pay their ongoing
obligations, including inability to
convert investments to cash despite
having a legal obligation to do so.
Source of Risk:
• Premium receivables
• Reinsurance exposures – i.e. reinsurers share of
liabilities, outstanding claims and commissions
• Bank deposits
• Corporate bonds and commercial papers
Mitigation:
• Internal credit policy of cash and carry for retail
customers coupled with a maximum of 60 days for
corporate credit. Additionally, provisions are made as
per IFRS 9 guidelines.
• Risk appetite limit that all reinsurance cessions are
made with parties that have a credit rating of at least
A- (by an Internationally recognised rating agency)
• Risk appetite limits for exposure to corporate bonds
and commercial papers.
